name: H5N1 bird flu
value: 3 cattle-linked US cases; no human spread
summary: Three Yakima County H5N1 cases in 2026, linked to dairy cattle, one fatal; no human-to-human spread found
state: ECDC reported on 3 Nov that two more Yakima County, Washington, residents were confirmed with H5N1 as of 1 Nov, one of whom died, making three cases in the county in 2026 (ECDC). The earlier October case followed occupational exposure to dairy cattle (Healio). Searches to 11 Nov found no newer human case or cluster, so these remain animal-to-human cases.
for_you: Risk to the public is rated low. People working with poultry or cattle should follow UKHSA or CDC guidance.

sources.title: ECDC — Avian influenza A(H5N1) human cases, United States, 2024–2026

why: H5N1 is the flu strain scientists most fear could become a pandemic; it has spread to mammals and dairy cattle.
drivers: Human cases, mammal-to-mammal spread, mutations, surveillance.
